messages.subject: Re: "High overlap" despite mutually exclusive conditions?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Eric,

Sorry for the delayed reply. I'm thinking you may have found a bug but I'm having a hard time reproducing it. Can you try running the following code, where "~/Desktop/test.txt" is your exact marker file from above and let me know what you get?

library(garnett)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)
 data(test_cds)
marker_check <- check_markers(test_cds,
                              "~/Desktop/test.txt",
                              db=org.Hs.eg.db,
                              cds_gene_id_type = "SYMBOL",
                              marker_file_gene_id_type = "SYMBOL")
plot_markers(marker_check)

Best,
Hannah

messages.subject: Re: marker file have 30 clusters
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jin,

I'm not sure why that would happen. What does your "check_markers" plot look like? I'm wondering if one of the cell types in your 30 cell type group is conflicting with the other cell types.

We've found that training and classifying on the same dataset works fine so long as you have good markers.

Best,
Hannah

On Sunday, August 25, 2019 at 9:56:15 AM UTC-4, Jin Ye wrote:
> Dear Garnett developers,
>
>    I have a maker file that has 30 cluster and a dataset with 38,000 cells. However, when I tried to train the classifier with this dataset, in the error message it says that I don't have enough cell for any cluster. If I use less cluster in the marker file (~10), it will work. May I ask what can I do in this case?
>
> And can I use the same dataset for both training dataset and classifying dataset since it is very difficult to find similar exiting dataset? Technically it's possible but what would be the potential disadvantages?
>
> Looking forward to your reply!!
>
> Best,
> Jin
messages.body_snippet:
Hi Jin,

I'm not sure why that would happen. What does your "check_markers" plot look like? I'm wondering if one of the cell types in your 30 cell type group is conflicting with the other cell types.
